summary:
[  edit  ]
The Mouse In  CHOP  outputs X and Y screen values for the mouse device and monitors the up/down state of the three mouse buttons.
When the Active flag is on, the Mouse X and Y positions are output through the channels named in the Position X and Y parameters and the button states are output through the channels named in the Left, Right and Middle Button parameters.
The button values are 0 for Button Up and 1 for Button Down.
The Mouse In  CHOP  and  Keyboard In CHOPs  are sometimes connected to the Position and Active inputs respectively of the  Record CHOP  to enable the recording of channels.

parameters.label: Active
parameters.name: active
parameters.description: ⊞  - While  On , the mouse movement will be output from and the  CHOP  will cook every frame. When set to  Off  it will not cook and the current mouse X or Y values will not be output.  While Playing  will capture mouse events only when the  Timeline  is playing forward.

parameters.label: Output Coordinates
parameters.name: output
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls the range of the mouse Position X and Position Y.

parameters.label: Normalized
parameters.name: normal
parameters.description: X and Y mouse positions are normalized to a range of 2 units per monitor. The primary monitor will be -1 to 1 with X=0 and Y=0 at the center of the monitor. Other monitors will be relative to these values. For example a monitor directly to the left of the primary monitor would have values in the range -1 on the right to -3 on the left of it.

parameters.label: Normalized Aspect
parameters.name: aspect
parameters.description: Following the same rules as Normalized, but normalized and adjusted to aspect ratio.

parameters.label: Absolute
parameters.name: absolute
parameters.description: Raw screen coordinates in pixel units. (0,0) is the bottom left of the primary monitor.

parameters.label: Position X
parameters.name: posxname
parameters.description: The name of the channel that returns the horizontal movement of the mouse.

parameters.label: Position Y
parameters.name: posyname
parameters.description: The name of the channel that returns the vertical movement of the mouse.

parameters.label: Left Button
parameters.name: lbuttonname
parameters.description: The name of the channel that returns the state of the left button.

parameters.label: Right Button
parameters.name: rbuttonname
parameters.description: The name of the channel that returns the state of the right button.

parameters.label: Middle Button
parameters.name: mbuttonname
parameters.description: The name of the channel that returns the state of the middle button.

parameters.label: Wheel
parameters.name: wheel
parameters.description: This channel goes up when the wheel is rolled away from the user and goes down when it is rolled the other way.

parameters.label: Wheel Increment
parameters.name: wheelinc
parameters.description: The amount that is added or subtracted to the current value of the Wheel channel when the wheel is moved.

parameters.label: Monitor
parameters.name: monitor
parameters.description: This channel returns which monitor the mouse cursor is currently on.

parameters.label: Panels
parameters.name: panels
parameters.description: Events are only triggered when the specified panel has focus.

parameters.label: Sample Rate
parameters.name: rate
parameters.description: The sample rate of the channels, in samples per second.

parameters.label: Extend Left
parameters.name: left
parameters.description: ⊞  - The left extend conditions (before/after range).

parameters.label: Hold

parameters.description: Hold the current value of the channel.

parameters.label: Slope
parameters.name: slope
parameters.description: Continue the slope before the start of the channel.

parameters.label: Cycle

parameters.description: Cycle the channel repeatedly.

parameters.label: Mirror

parameters.label: Extend Right

parameters.description: ⊞  - The right extend conditions (before/after range).

parameters.label: Hold
parameters.name: hold
parameters.description: Hold the current value of the channel.

parameters.label: Slope
parameters.name: slope
parameters.description: Continue the slope after the end of the channel.

parameters.label: Cycle
parameters.name: cycle
parameters.description: Cycle the channel repeatedly.

parameters.label: Mirror

parameters.description: Cycle the channel repeatedly, mirroring every other cycle.

parameters.label: Default Value

parameters.label: Time Slice
parameters.name: timeslice
parameters.description: Turning this on forces the channels to be " Time Sliced ".  A  Time Slice  is the time between the last cook frame and the current cook frame.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: To determine which channels get affected, some CHOPs use a  Scope  string on the Common page.

parameters.label: Sample Rate  Match
parameters.name: srselect
parameters.description: ⊞  - Handle cases where multiple input CHOPs' sample rates are different. When Resampling occurs, the curves are interpolated according to the Interpolation Method Option, or "Linear" if the Interpolate Options are not available.

parameters.label: Resample At First Input's Rate

parameters.label: Error If Rates Differ

parameters.label: Export  Method

parameters.label: DAT  Table by Name

parameters.label: samples
parameters.description: per-second of a  CHOP . Each CHOP in your network has a sample rate. In contrast, the overall timeline has a  Frame Rate , which is the number of frames to  cook  and display per second, generally your monitor display frequency, default 60.

parameters.description: line text or tables. Multi-line text is often a python  Script  or  GLSL  Shader, but can be any multi-line text.  Tables  are rows and columns of cells, each containing a text string.
